text: To prove a biconditional P ↔ Q one proves two implications: the forward direction P → Q and its ___, the implication Q → P.
explanation: A biconditional P ↔ Q holds iff both P → Q and Q → P hold, and Q → P is the converse of P → Q. Proving only one of the two directions is the most common error in biconditional proofs.
